abstract_sentences.text: Recent progress in large-scale robotic datasets and vision-language models (VLMs) has advanced research on vision-language-action (VLA) models.

evidence.anchor: Recent progress in large-scale robotic datasets

abstract_sentences.text: However, existing VLA models still face two fundamental challenges: (i) producing precise low-level actions from high-dimensional observations, (ii) bridging domain gaps across heterogeneous data sources, including diverse robot embodiments and human demonstrations.

Existing methods often encode latent variables from either visual dynamics or robotic actions to guide policy learning, but they fail to fully exploit the complementary multi-modal knowledge present in large-scale, heterogeneous datasets.
In this work, we present X Robotic Model 1 (XR-1), a novel framework for versatile and scalable VLA learning across diverse robots, tasks, and environments.
At its core, XR-1 introduces the Unified Vision-Motion Codes (UVMC), a discrete latent representation learned via a dual-branch VQ-VAE that jointly encodes visual dynamics and robotic motion.

UVMC addresses these challenges by (i) serving as an intermediate representation between the observations and actions, and (ii) aligning multimodal dynamic information from heterogeneous data sources to capture complementary knowledge.

To effectively exploit UVMC, we propose a three-stage training paradigm: (i) self-supervised UVMC learning, (ii) UVMC-guided pretraining on large-scale cross-embodiment robotic datasets, and (iii) task-specific post-training.
We validate XR-1 through extensive real-world experiments with more than 14,000 rollouts on six different robot embodiments, spanning over 120 diverse manipulation tasks.

XR-1 consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines such as π0.5, π0, RDT, UniVLA, and GR00T-N1.5 while demonstrating strong generalization to novel objects, background variations, distractors, and illumination changes.

experimental_design.name: Predeclared research questions
experimental_design.description: Section 4 enumerates four questions: SOTA comparison, pretraining/fast adaptation, OOD generalization, and component/training effects.

experimental_design.name: Real-world embodiments and task setup
experimental_design.description: Six embodiments; each has 20 tasks, parallel grippers, calibrated multi-view cameras, and teleoperated expert demonstrations with RGB/proprioception.

experimental_design.name: Training stages and data sources
experimental_design.description: UVMC pretraining uses RoboMIND, Open-X, XR-D, and Ego4D; policy pretraining uses XR-D; task fine-tuning targets tasks.

experimental_design.name: Baseline set and implementation note
experimental_design.description: The named baselines are π0.5, π0, RDT, UniVLA, and GR00T-N1.5; the π0 result uses original JAX due to reported Lerobot degradation.

experimental_design.name: Real-world aggregation and denominator
experimental_design.description: The paper evaluates 20 rollouts per task and reports human-evaluated success rates; tables average across tasks.

experimental_design.name: OOD conditions
experimental_design.description: Novel objects, dynamic/static distractors, illumination, and background variations are evaluated on Dual-Arm Franka scenarios.

experimental_design.name: Out-of-box comparison condition
experimental_design.description: Stage-2 XR-1 is evaluated without Stage-3 on seven Franka tasks; baselines are fine-tuned on those tasks.

experimental_design.name: Fast-adaptation condition
experimental_design.description: For Tien Kung 2.0, 15 unseen tasks have 20 trajectories each; XR-1 is joint-task while ACT/DP are single-task.

experimental_design.name: Simulation condition
experimental_design.description: CALVIN D→D uses language-conditioned long-horizon tasks across four environments.

experimental_design.name: Hyperparameters and compute
experimental_design.description: Tables 5–7 and Appendix B.3 give batch sizes, steps, architecture, GPU-hours, GPU type, and inference rate.

claim_closure.claim: A three-stage UVMC framework can raise task-level VLA success across the evaluated robots.
claim_closure.method_response: Dual-branch VQ-VAE, UVMC prediction tokens, and task fine-tuning in §3.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Six-embodiment task tables, OOD, OOB, adaptation, and ablation evidence in §4 and Appendices D–F.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 restates the three-stage framework and multi-robot performance.

claim_closure.claim: UVMC and alignment contribute beyond action-only or vision-only features.
claim_closure.method_response: Shared quantization and KL alignment specify the claimed components.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 3 and Table 14 compare modality variants, w/o KL, and codebook choices.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion repeats UVMC as the central abstraction but does not isolate each component there.

claim_closure.claim: The learned representation transfers across embodiments.
claim_closure.origin: Introduction claim of embodiment-agnostic consistency, p. 2.
claim_closure.method_response: UVMC shares a codebook and alignment target across data sources.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Unseen Tien Kung 2.0 results, Table 16 CrossRobot, and retrieval/t-SNE diagnostic figures.

claim_closure.claim: Ego4D human video improves the reported policy result.
claim_closure.method_response: Human-only data use the visual reconstruction objective in §3.2.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 15 changes only Ego4D inclusion in a 10% Stage-1 setup and reports 38.3 versus 32.5 task average.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion refers to heterogeneous sources generally, not a separate Ego4D result.

claim_closure.claim: XR-1 generalizes to unseen environmental conditions.
claim_closure.method_response: No separate mechanism beyond the UVMC training recipe is isolated for each shift.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 4 covers six listed shifts and compares only π0.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 generalizes the claim to environments and task demands.

claim_closure.claim: UVMC captures the causal link between seeing and acting.
claim_closure.origin: Related Work claims existing paradigms miss the causal link, p. 3.
claim_closure.method_response: The model couples vision and motion through codebook and KL losses.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Ablations, retrieval, and t-SNE show associations and performance differences.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion uses alignment language, not a causal identification result.

rhetoric_analysis.basis: Case-insensitive exact phrase search in the p.1–10 PDF text; PDF hyphenation makes this a coarse audit.
rhetoric_analysis.interpretation: The phrasing foregrounds new components and broad performance claims; qualifiers occur mostly around deployment or impact.

final_judgment.single_storyline: UVMC is presented as a shared discrete interface that lets a VLA borrow visual dynamics from human video and motion grounding from robot data, then transfer through three-stage training.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The framework figure, the input/output definition, numbered losses, main six-robot protocol, one full unseen-embodiment table, a main ablation, OOD/OOB/fast-adaptation evidence, and a compact conclusion.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Architecture/hyperparameters/compute, detailed source rows, full results matrices, codebook/Ego4D/cross-robot ablations, CALVIN, retrieval/t-SNE, failures, and the full task specification. This migration keeps the central recipe legible but makes reproducibility and task-distribution audit appendix-dependent.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2 plus equations (1)–(3) and Table 3 form a compact mechanism-to-ablation chain; the explicit Stage 1/2/3 rows let readers locate the proposed source of improvement.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The paper calls UVMC causal and embodiment-agnostic, but evidence is descriptive success-rate comparison, ablation, retrieval, and t-SNE without seed-level uncertainty or a causal identification design.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a multi-modal intermediate representation, show the system graph, formal objective, component ablation, and an out-of-distribution task in the main causal path; explicitly call the appendix for full matrices and implementation evidence.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: Use this rule for systems whose central claim is an implementable representation/training recipe. Theory, datasets, user studies, and deployment papers need proof, data-governance, study-design, or operational evidence at the corresponding boundary.
